Before and after the change, `uv run pytest -q` printed `24 passed`. Two candidate commit messages:

- A: `Refactor`
- B: `Extract is_wanted from total_by_category`

parts.prompt_md: What does this change do?
parts.model_answer_md: It moves the rule for which expenses count (matching category, amount at least the minimum) out of the loop into its own function, `is_wanted`, and calls it from `total_by_category`, with the same results.
rubric: Says the filtering condition is moved into a named function `is_wanted` that `total_by_category` now calls, without changing results
parts.weak_answers_md: "It adds a function" is too thin: the mark is for saying which logic moved (the category and minimum filter) and that the results stay the same. Answers that say it "changes how expenses are filtered" miss that the 24 unedited tests pass: nothing about the filtering changed.

parts.prompt_md: Which message is better, and why? Answer from the point of view of someone reading the history six months later.
parts.model_answer_md: B. It says what moved and where, so a reader can find the commit that created `is_wanted` and knows the behaviour should not have changed. A says only that something was restructured, somewhere.
rubric: Chooses B
Reason from the later reader's view: B names what changed (the function and where it came from), A gives nothing to search or check
parts.weak_answers_md: Choosing B "because it is longer" misses the reason. Answers that prefer A "because it shows it is a refactoring" ignore that B also implies no behaviour change, and says what was done.

parts.prompt_md: Name one test you can now write that was awkward before, in words.
parts.model_answer_md: A test that calls `is_wanted` with a single 10.00 dining expense, category `"dining"` and minimum `10.0`, and checks it returns `True`, pinning down that an amount equal to the minimum is kept.

Which refactoring move is this, and what does it make possible?

options.text_md: Extract constant: the report's fixed text now sits in one list, so each label changes in one place
options.why_md: Nothing gets a name: the strings are the same literals, now appended to a list. Extract constant was `5e9466d`, where `40` became `RULE_WIDTH`.

options.text_md: Introduce a parameter object / type: the report is now a `list[str]`, so mypy can check each line
options.why_md: No new type is defined, and there are no hints yet (they arrive in `04d699f`). Introduce a type was `017f926`, where the tuple became `Expense`.

questions.explanation_md: This is `9d6c607`, the session 7 row "`run()` split into read, compute, format". Before, `run()` built the report and printed it line by line, so checking the report meant running the program and looking at the screen. On the sample data the printed report is identical (we ran both commits); what moved is where the printing happens. options.why_md: It copies the table without reading the function: the values are counts, so `int`. We ran it: `Incompatible return value type (got "dict[str, int]", expected "dict[str, float]")`.

A new file in the group's repository, and the first strict run on it:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Expense:
    date: str
    merchant: str
    category: str
    amount: float


def total_for(expenses, day):
    return sum(e.amount for e in expenses if e.date == day)


def day_line(expenses: list[Expense], day: str) -> str:
    return f"{day}: {total_for(expenses, day):.2f}"


def busiest(expenses: list[Expense], days: list[str]) -> float:
    return max(total_for(expenses, day) for day in days)
```

```console
$ uv run mypy --strict src
src/tracker/daily.py:12: error: Function is missing a type annotation  [no-untyped-def]
src/tracker/daily.py:17: error: Call to untyped function "total_for" in typed context  [no-untyped-call]
src/tracker/daily.py:21: error: Returning Any from function declared to return "float"  [no-any-return]
src/tracker/daily.py:21: error: Call to untyped function "total_for" in typed context  [no-untyped-call]
Found 4 errors in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

How do you work through the four errors?

options.text_md: Fix line 21 first, because `Returning Any` is the most serious, and change the return type to `Any`
options.why_md: `Any` would make the message go away and switch off the checking of every caller. And the `Any` comes from line 12's missing signature.

options.text_md: Start at the last line and move up, since the newest errors are the ones that stopped mypy
options.why_md: mypy reports every error it finds; it does not stop at the last one. The cause is higher up, where the function is defined.

options.text_md: Give `total_for` a signature on line 12 and run mypy again; the other three should disappear
options.why_md: Right: line 12 is the first error and the cause. Lines 17 and 21 are calls to a function mypy cannot see inside, and the `Any` on line 21 comes from its unknown result.

options.text_md: Add `# type: ignore` to lines 17 and 21 first, to see which errors are real
options.why_md: That hides evidence before reading it. Fixing the cause on line 12 shows which errors are left, at no cost.

questions.explanation_md: Session 7's method: read the first error, find its cause, fix it, run again. Line 12 is the cause: `total_for` has no signature. Line 17 and line 21 are calls to it from typed code, and line 21 also returns the unknown `Any` that comes out of it. With `(expenses: list[Expense], day: str) -> float` added to line 12, we ran mypy again and it printed `Success: no issues found in 1 source file`.
